body:
**Task ID:** `t2038` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~30m`
**Logged:** 2026-04-13
**Tags:** `research` `ci` `interactive`

## Description

research: pick path to bypass branch protection for github-actions[bot] — rulesets vs fine-grained PAT — research/decide task; deliverable is a documented decision + AGENTS.md update + child implementation task. Two viable paths for unblocking `github-actions[bot]` pushes to main: (1) migrate classic protection to GitHub Rulesets with `bypass_actors` containing `github-actions` (~2-3h one-time, no ongoing cost, future-proof since GitHub is sunsetting classic protection); (2) fine-grained PAT stored as a repo secret (~30m one-time, ongoing rotation cost, secret management surface). Picking the wrong one creates either ongoing rotation fatigue or a moderately risky migration. Belongs to maintainer judgment on threat model, not LLM guess. Task starts with a 30-second curl test to verify GitHub hasn't silently fixed `bypass_pull_request_allowances` on classic protection since 2026-04-13 — if it has, problem disappears. Reasoning tier because deliverable is a recommendation with rationale (Sonnet enumerates without committing). Implementation is a downstream child task filed by t2038 itself. Until both ship, every merged PR with a tNNN title hits the t2029 loud-failure path and requires manual `task-complete-helper.sh`.

## Task Brief


<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
# t2038: research: pick path to bypass branch protection for github-actions[bot] — rulesets vs fine-grained PAT

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-13
- **Session:** OpenCode:interactive (gap-closing pass that shipped t2015/t2018/t2027–t2030/t2034)
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** During the gap-closing session I shipped t2029 (make `sync-on-pr-merge` push failure visible) + t2034 (add GH_TOKEN to the PR comment fallback). Together they convert a silent 3-week failure into a loud one with a user-friendly manual fallback. **They are NOT a fix for the root cause.** The root cause: classic branch protection on personal-account public repos cannot bypass `required_pull_request_reviews` for `github-actions[bot]` — confirmed by direct API test (HTTP 500 on PATCH `bypass_pull_request_allowances`). Until the real fix ships, every merged PR with a TODO entry continues to fire the loud-failure path and require a manual `task-complete-helper.sh` call. Two viable real-fix paths exist with very different trade-offs. This task picks the path BEFORE writing any implementation.

## What

A documented decision (recorded in this brief's "Decision" section, plus a comment in `.agents/AGENTS.md` and a follow-up implementation brief) on which of the two paths to take for unblocking `github-actions[bot]` pushes to main:

1. **Migrate classic branch protection to GitHub Rulesets** with `bypass_actors` containing `github-actions`.
2. **Set up a fine-grained PAT** stored as a repo secret, used by the relevant workflows for the push.

Out of scope for this task: the actual implementation of whichever path is chosen. That is a downstream task (t2039 or whatever the next available ID is) filed by this task as part of its deliverable.

End-state: a decision note in the brief, an updated AGENTS.md "Known limitation" paragraph reflecting the chosen path, and a child implementation task ready to dispatch.

## Why

**Why this is a research task and not an implementation task.** The two paths have non-trivially different cost profiles, security surfaces, and ongoing maintenance burdens. Picking the wrong one creates either ongoing rotation fatigue (PAT) or a moderately risky migration that needs to preserve every existing classic protection rule (rulesets). The decision belongs to the maintainer, not to an LLM working off a one-line hint.

**Why it's worth doing now and not deferring indefinitely.** The t2029+t2034 fix makes the failure VISIBLE but does not REMOVE the friction. Every merged PR with a tNNN title currently produces:

1. A failed workflow step in the Actions UI (visible noise)
2. A `<!-- t2029:auto-complete-blocked -->` comment on the PR (additional noise)
3. A required manual `task-complete-helper.sh tNNN --pr NNN` call from the maintainer's local machine

Multiplied across the ~5-15 PRs/day this repo currently ships, the maintainer is paying ~10-30 manual command-runs per day. That's the daily cost of NOT picking a path. Even the worse path (PAT) eliminates this friction in ~30 minutes of setup.

**Why the decision matters for the security boundary.** Classic protection's `enforce_admins: false` already lets human admins bypass via `--admin` merge. The question is who else gets that power:

- **Rulesets path**: `github-actions` (the GitHub Actions app, including ALL workflows in this repo) gets bypass. Trust boundary becomes "every workflow file in `.github/workflows/`". Admin = me only, app bypass = all repo workflows.
- **PAT path**: The PAT identity (a specific user, e.g., me) gets bypass. Trust boundary becomes "anyone who can read the secret". Stored secret implies anyone with `contents: write` on the repo can exfiltrate it via a malicious workflow PR.

Both paths broaden the bypass list beyond just human admin. The question is which broadening is safer — and "safer" here is a maintainer judgment about repository threat model, not a technical fact.

## Tier

### Tier checklist

- [ ] **≤2 files to modify?** — research task; the deliverable is a decision + AGENTS.md note + child implementation task. Three artifacts.
- [ ] **Complete code blocks for every edit?** — N/A, this is research.
- [ ] **No judgment or design decisions?** — judgment is the entire point.
- [ ] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?** — error path is "what if neither option works on a personal-account repo", which needs to be explored.
- [x] **≤1h estimate?** — actually 2-3h: 30-60m research + 30-60m write-up + 30m draft-implementation-brief.
- [x] **≤4 acceptance criteria?** — exactly 4

**Selected tier:** `tier:reasoning`

**Tier rationale:** Research/decide tasks live in the reasoning tier because they require:
1. **Reading external documentation** (GitHub Rulesets docs, fine-grained PAT scoping rules, classic-vs-rulesets feature parity matrix).
2. **Holding multiple viable paths in mind simultaneously** while comparing trade-offs across security, ongoing cost, migration risk, and feature parity.
3. **Recommending a specific path with rationale** that the maintainer can either accept or reject without re-doing the research.
4. **Drafting a child implementation brief** that's executable at a lower tier once the path is chosen.

Sonnet COULD do this but would tend toward enumerating options without committing. Opus is more likely to land on a specific recommendation. Reserve this for the higher tier.

## How (Approach)

### Phase 1: Research (~30-60 minutes)

**1.1 Verify the current limitation is real and not a configuration error.**

```bash
# Confirm the HTTP 500 reproduces (this was the t2029 finding)
cat > /tmp/bypass.json <<'EOF'
{
  "dismiss_stale_reviews": true,
  "require_code_owner_reviews": false,
  "required_approving_review_count": 1,
  "bypass_pull_request_allowances": {
    "users": [],
    "teams": [],
    "apps": ["github-actions"]
  }
}
EOF
curl -sS -i -X PATCH "https://api.github.com/repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gh auth token)" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -d @/tmp/bypass.json
```

If this returns HTTP 500 with empty body (as it did on 2026-04-13), classic-protection bypass is genuinely unsupported on this plan. If it returns 200 OK, GitHub silently fixed the limitation and Path 0 ("just use the bypass list") becomes available — short-circuit the rest of this task.

**1.2 Research GitHub Rulesets feature parity with classic protection.**

Read:

- <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets>
- <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/creating-rulesets-for-a-repository>
- <https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules>

Verify rulesets support EVERY rule currently in classic protection on this repo:

```bash
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/branches/main/protection" --jq '
  {
    required_status_checks: .required_status_checks.contexts,
    required_pull_request_reviews: .required_pull_request_reviews,
    required_signatures: .required_signatures.enabled,
    enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled,
    required_linear_history: .required_linear_history.enabled,
    allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled,
    allow_deletions: .allow_deletions.enabled,
    required_conversation_resolution: .required_conversation_resolution.enabled,
    lock_branch: .lock_branch.enabled,
    allow_fork_syncing: .allow_fork_syncing.enabled,
    block_creations: .block_creations.enabled,
    restrictions: .restrictions
  }
'
```

For each present rule, find the equivalent rule type in rulesets (`rules` array). If any rule has no equivalent, that's a blocker for the rulesets path — flag it as a finding.

**1.3 Research fine-grained PAT capabilities.**

Read:

- <https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens>
- <https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/permissions-required-for-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens>

Verify:

- A fine-grained PAT scoped to a single repo with `Contents: Write` permission can push to main when the user identity has admin bypass via `enforce_admins: false`. (Test by creating a throwaway PAT and trying a no-op push.)
- The PAT can be stored as a repo Actions secret and consumed by the relevant workflows.
- The PAT respects `secret_scanning` so accidental commits don't leak it.

**1.4 Identify rotation cost and threat model differences.**

For each path, document:

- Setup time (one-time)
- Ongoing rotation cost (yearly, monthly, never)
- Failure mode if the credential expires unnoticed (loud vs silent)
- Worst-case compromise impact (what can an attacker do if they get the credential)

### Phase 2: Decision Write-Up (~30-60 minutes)

In this brief's "Decision" section below, document:

- **The chosen path** (rulesets / PAT / neither viable).
- **Why** this path was preferred (security, cost, future-proofing).
- **What was rejected** about the other path.
- **Failure mode** if the chosen path doesn't work as expected (rollback plan).

### Phase 3: Child Implementation Task (~30 minutes)

File a downstream task implementing the chosen path:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
  --repo-path /Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops \
  --title "<implementation title for chosen path>"
```

Write the child implementation brief at the appropriate tier (likely `tier:standard` for either path). Reference t2038's decision section in the child brief's "Context & Decisions".

Then update `.agents/AGENTS.md`'s "Known limitation — sync-on-pr-merge TODO auto-completion (t2029)" paragraph to reflect:

- Which path was chosen
- The child implementation task ID and PR number (when available)

### Verification

```bash
# Decision is documented
grep -c "## Decision" todo/tasks/t2038-brief.md  # expect ≥1

# Child task ID exists
grep -E "Implementation task: t[0-9]+" todo/tasks/t2038-brief.md

# AGENTS.md updated to point at the chosen path
grep "Known limitation — sync-on-pr-merge" .agents/AGENTS.md | grep -E "(rulesets|fine-grained PAT)"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The brief contains a `## Decision` section naming the chosen path with explicit rationale.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "^## Decision"
    path: "todo/tasks/t2038-brief.md"
  ```
- [x] A child implementation task is filed with its own task ID and brief.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Implementation task: t[0-9]+"
    path: "todo/tasks/t2038-brief.md"
  ```
- [x] `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Known limitation" paragraph references the chosen path and the child task ID.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Known limitation.*sync-on-pr-merge.*(rulesets|fine-grained PAT)"
    path: ".agents/AGENTS.md"
  ```
- [x] The classic-protection HTTP 500 limitation is verified still present (or documented as resolved by GitHub).
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Re-run the curl PATCH call from Phase 1.1. If it returns HTTP 500, the limitation persists. If it returns 200 OK, document that GitHub silently fixed it and short-circuit the rest of the task."
  ```

## Decision

**Chosen path: fine-grained PAT (Path B)**

**Implementation task:** `t2048` — `implement: fine-grained PAT path for github-actions[bot] main push (from t2038 decision)` — GH#18643

**Failure-mode rollback:** Revoke the PAT in GitHub UI and unset the `SYNC_PAT` secret. The workflow immediately falls back to the t2029/t2034 loud-failure path (visible workflow error + PR comment with the manual `task-complete-helper.sh` command). No branch-protection state change to roll back.

### Research findings

**Phase 1.1 — HTTP 500 reproduces (2026-04-13, 16:41Z).**
`PATCH /repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/branches/main/protection/required_pull_request_reviews` with `bypass_pull_request_allowances.apps: ["github-actions"]` still returns `HTTP/2 500` with empty body on this personal-account public repo. `x-github-request-id: F2C4:482FE:BBC65B9:A3BB5F9:69DD0EA9`. Path 0 ("just use the existing classic-protection bypass list") remains unavailable. The limitation is not a configuration error — `bypass_pull_request_allowances` is genuinely unsupported on this plan.

**Phase 1.2 — Rulesets feature parity is fine, but Integration bypass is blocked for personal repos.**
Current classic protection has 3 rules that need an equivalent in rulesets: `required_status_checks` (3 contexts — `review-bot-gate`, `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`, `Complexity Analysis`), `required_pull_request_reviews` (1 approval, dismiss-stale), and nothing else non-default. All three map cleanly to ruleset rule types (`required_status_checks`, `pull_request`). No feature-parity blockers.

**But the critical finding:** creating a ruleset with `bypass_actors: [{actor_type: "Integration", actor_id: 15368}]` (GitHub Actions app) on this personal-account repo fails with:

```
422 Validation Failed
Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization
```

Personal repos have no "owner organization", so GitHub App integrations cannot be added as bypass actors. **This disqualifies the originally-proposed Path 1 (rulesets + Integration bypass) entirely on personal-account repos.**

What _did_ work in testing (verified by creating + deleting disposable rulesets):

- `RepositoryRole` bypass actors (role IDs 2, 4, 5 — write/maintain/admin). Accepted, but `github-actions[bot]` has no repo role that would trigger the bypass — it authenticates as the special github-actions app, not as a user with a role.
- `DeployKey` bypass actor with `actor_id: 0`. Accepted. Any push via a repo deploy key would bypass the rule. This surfaced an unanticipated **Path C**: migrate to rulesets + add a deploy key + change the workflow to push over SSH.

**Phase 1.3 — Fine-grained PAT capabilities.**
A fine-grained PAT scoped to a single repo with `Contents: Write` authenticates as the owning user. When that user is an admin and classic protection has `enforce_admins: false` (current state), the push is evaluated under the admin role and bypasses `required_approving_review_count`. No ruleset migration needed. The PAT must have a ≤366-day expiration (no "never expires" option for fine-grained PATs as of 2026-04) and is stored as an Actions secret (`SYNC_PAT`) consumed by the `checkout` and `push` steps of the `sync-on-pr-merge` job. Recursion is prevented by the existing `[skip ci]` tag on the commit message.

**Phase 1.4 — Threat model + rotation cost.**

| Dimension | Path B (fine-grained PAT) | Path C (rulesets + deploy key) |
|---|---|---|
| Setup time | ~20-30m | ~2-3h (ruleset migration + key gen + SSH workflow change) |
| Ongoing rotation | ~15m/year (PAT max 366d) | zero (SSH keys do not expire) |
| Migration risk | none — classic protection untouched | moderate — must preserve 3 status checks + PR rule + dismiss-stale in new ruleset, 1-step rollback possible |
| Credential scope | single repo (`Contents:Write`) | single repo (deploy key with write) |
| Credential trust boundary | "anyone who can read the `SYNC_PAT` secret" | "anyone who can read the SSH private key secret" — identical |
| Expiry failure mode | loud — push fails → t2029+t2034 fallback fires (error annotation + PR comment) | loud — same fallback fires if ruleset is misconfigured |
| Future-proofing | classic protection may deprecate; would force eventual rulesets migration | already on the forward-looking rulesets track |

**Phase 2 — Why Path B.**

1. **Setup cost asymmetry.** 20-30m vs 2-3h is ~6-9× cheaper for identical immediate benefit (eliminating the ~10-30 manual `task-complete-helper.sh` calls/day created by the t2029 loud-failure path). The "no rotation" benefit of Path C is worth ~15m/year, which would take ~8-10 years to amortise the extra 2h of up-front work — well past the half-life of this repo's workflow file.
2. **Rollback simplicity.** Path B's rollback is one secret revoke. Path C's rollback requires restoring classic protection state, re-enabling the deploy key's previous state, and reverting the workflow's SSH changes. In a break-glass scenario (e.g., key compromise), Path B is fewer steps under stress.
3. **The rotation failure mode is already solved.** Path C's pitch is "no rotation = no silent breakage", but t2029+t2034 already turned PAT expiry into a loud, self-announcing failure (workflow annotation + PR comment + exact manual command). The hidden-silent-failure cost that motivates "no rotation" doesn't exist here.
4. **Future-proofing pays later, not now.** GitHub has announced rulesets as the future but has NOT announced a classic-protection sunset date. Doing the migration now is speculative work — better to wait until GitHub forces the migration, at which point Path C (or `RepositoryRole` + admin PAT) becomes the natural choice. No reason to eat the migration cost twice.
5. **Threat model is identical.** Both paths store a long-lived credential with write access to this repo as an Actions secret. Neither is meaningfully "more secure" — the attack is the same: compromise a workflow that can read secrets. Path B is simpler to reason about because its identity (PAT owner = admin user) is also the identity that already has direct-push capability.

**Path C (rulesets + deploy key) remains a reasonable _later_ migration target** when GitHub eventually deprecates classic protection or when PAT rotation becomes annoying enough to justify the migration. At that point, t2038 can be re-opened to file a new decision task, or the rulesets migration can be folded into a broader infrastructure refresh.

**Path A (rulesets + github-actions Integration bypass): disqualified.** The 422 error on Integration bypass actors for personal-account repos makes this path unbuildable without migrating the repo to an organization first — a disruption out of all proportion to the problem being solved.

### Threat-model note on PAT scope

The fine-grained PAT must be scoped as narrowly as possible:

- **Repository access:** only `marcusquinn/aidevops` (no `all repositories` selector).
- **Repository permissions:** only `Contents: Read and write`. Explicitly NOT `Workflows: Write` (which would let the PAT modify workflow files, broadening the blast radius for a compromised secret).
- **Expiration:** ≤366 days. Calendar reminder at day 330 to rotate.
- **Storage:** Actions secret named `SYNC_PAT` on this repo only. Not shared across repos.
- **Owner identity:** `marcusquinn` (repo admin). When the PAT pushes, the commit author is the workflow identity but the authenticated principal is the admin user, which bypasses PR-review requirements via `enforce_admins: false`.

The 6 non-admin collaborators (`vladimirdulov`, `alex-solovyev`, `zzhovo`, `optimizewp`, `Bartek532`, `B-Novembit`) do NOT gain push-to-main capability from this change — their identities are unchanged, and the PAT identity is admin-only.

## Context & Decisions (research-time)

**Why a research task instead of just picking one and implementing it.** I noted both paths in my session summary as "tracked for later, neither fits this session's budget". But "tracked for later" is invisible without a brief. The user explicitly asked whether to file a TODO for this — meaning they want the decision visible and dispatchable, not buried in a session summary.

**Why tier:reasoning instead of standard.** Two reasons. (1) The deliverable is a decision with rationale, which Sonnet tends to enumerate without committing — Opus is more likely to land on a specific recommendation. (2) The implementation that follows from the decision is downstream (a child task), so this task's value is concentrated entirely in the quality of the chosen path, not the volume of work done.

**Why include the "verify HTTP 500 still reproduces" step.** GitHub frequently relaxes API limitations between versions. If `bypass_pull_request_allowances` started working on personal-account public repos between when I tested (2026-04-13) and when this task is dispatched, the entire problem disappears and Path 0 ("just use the existing bypass field") becomes the trivially correct answer. Re-verifying is 30 seconds of work and saves potentially hours of unnecessary migration.

**Threat model context for the decision.** This repo has 6 non-admin collaborators with `push` permission (vladimirdulov, alex-solovyev, zzhovo, optimizewp, Bartek532, B-Novembit). The `required_approving_review_count: 1` rule exists primarily to prevent these collaborators from pushing directly to main without review. Any bypass mechanism we add must NOT widen the bypass list to include these accounts. Both rulesets and PAT can be scoped narrowly enough to satisfy this — but verifying the scoping is part of the research.

**Non-goals (research-time):**

- Picking a third option (e.g., GitHub App with installation-scoped credentials). That's worth exploring only if both rulesets AND PAT have disqualifying issues, which would be surprising.
- Implementing the chosen path. That's the child task.
- Updating any workflow files in this repo.
- Rotating any existing PATs.

## Relevant Files

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml:507-563` — the t2029+t2034 loud-failure block whose root cause this task addresses.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Known limitation — sync-on-pr-merge TODO auto-completion (t2029)" — the paragraph to update once a path is chosen.
- `todo/tasks/t2029-brief.md` — context on why the silent-failure-fix was scoped narrowly.
- `todo/tasks/t2034-brief.md` — context on the GH_TOKEN follow-up that completes the visible-failure path.
- <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets>
- <https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens>

title: t2043: fix: npm publish workflow broken by self-replacing npm install
body:
Root cause: `Update npm for Trusted Publishers` step in publish-packages.yml runs `npm install -g npm@latest` which self-replaces the running npm, half-completes, and dies with `Cannot find module 'promise-retry'`. Last successful npm publish was v3.5.896 (2026-04-03); 100+ releases failed since. README badge correctly shows npm version but is ~400 versions stale because npm is stuck. Fix: bump Setup Node to node-version 24 (ships npm 11.5+ which natively supports OIDC Trusted Publishers) and replace the self-replacing install step with a version assertion.

Now that t2043 unblocked the publish-npm job, the second job (`update-homebrew-tap`) is running and failing at the `Sync Homebrew formula back to repo` step. It runs `git push origin HEAD:main` from a GHA runner using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is rejected by branch protection (`GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main. Changes must be made through a pull request.`). Evidence: run 24325147206 (v3.8.3). Fix options: (a) open a PR via `gh pr create` and merge with admin bypass, (b) use a fine-grained PAT in a secret with bypass permission, (c) move the homebrew formula sync to a release-time PR rather than a direct push, (d) drop the in-repo sync and only push to the marcusquinn/homebrew-tap repo (the `Push to homebrew-tap repo` step that follows is the actual publication path). Recommended: option (d) — the in-repo `homebrew/aidevops.rb` is just a template; the real consumer is the homebrew-tap repo. The intermediate `Sync Homebrew formula back to repo` is redundant. EDIT: `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` lines 113-125 — remove the `Sync Homebrew formula back to repo` step.

title: consolidated: 3 Gemini review findings in pulse-merge.sh from PR #18379 — already resolved via PR #18602
body:
_Supersedes #18587 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Three medium-priority Gemini code review findings on `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` that were left unaddressed when PR #18379 was merged. All three have since been resolved via PR #18602 (merged 2026-04-13T04:33:38Z).

## Why

PR #18379 (t1972: Phase 4 — extract pr-gates + merge cycle into pulse-merge.sh) was merged with unaddressed Gemini bot feedback. The review scanner auto-filed #18587 to track these. A subsequent worker verified that a parallel fix PR (#18602) had already landed on `main` before this issue was processed.

## How

**Status: Already resolved. No implementation action required.**

The three Gemini findings were:

### Finding 1 — Health counters updated in subshell (medium)

Health counters were updated within a function typically called via `run_stage_with_timeout` in `pulse-wrapper.sh`. Updates inside a subshell are invisible to the parent process.

**Resolution (per @milohiss):** Fixed in `pulse-merge.sh` lines 532–537. Counter deltas are now written to a temp file (`pulse-health-merge-$$.tmp`) instead of updating subshell-invisible global variables. The parent reads this file after `run_stage_with_timeout` returns.

### Finding 2 — Hardcoded path to `gh-signature-helper.sh` (medium)

The path to `gh-signature-helper.sh` was hardcoded, inconsistent with other scripts that use `AGENTS_DIR`.

**Resolution (per @milohiss):** Fixed in `pulse-merge.sh` lines 781–785. Now uses `${AGENTS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/agents}/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` via a `_sig_helper` local variable.

### Finding 3 — Hardcoded `sha=main` as default branch (medium)

The GitHub API was called with `sha=main` hardcoded, which fails on repos with a different default branch.

**Resolution (per @milohiss):** Fixed in `pulse-merge.sh` lines 990–993. The `-f sha=main` flag was removed; the GitHub API now uses the repository's actual default branch.

All three fixes were merged via **PR #18602** (commit `139ebdc19`), which also closed duplicate issue **#18571**.

### Verification

```bash
# Verify finding 1 fix (temp file pattern)
grep -n 'pulse-health-merge.*\.tmp' .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh

# Verify finding 2 fix (AGENTS_DIR used for signature helper)
grep -n 'AGENTS_DIR.*gh-signature-helper' .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh

# Verify finding 3 fix (sha=main removed)
! grep -n 'sha=main' .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Health counter temp file pattern present in pulse-merge.sh (lines ~532–537)
- [x] `AGENTS_DIR` used for gh-signature-helper.sh path (lines ~781–785)
- [x] No hardcoded `sha=main` in pulse-merge.sh (lines ~990–993)
- [x] All fixes confirmed merged via PR #18602

**All criteria already met.** This issue is filed as a record only.

## Context & Decisions

- **per @gemini-code-assist (PR #18379 review):** Three medium-priority findings identified in pulse-merge.sh: subshell counter update isolation, hardcoded helper path, and hardcoded default branch. See PR #18379 review comment for full details.
- **per @milohiss (comment on #18587):** Verified that all three findings are already addressed in `main` as of PR #18602 (merged 2026-04-13). Issue #18587 is a duplicate of #18571 which is already resolved. No further action needed.
- **Decision:** Close as already-resolved duplicate. The consolidated issue serves as a record of the review findings and their resolution path.

## Contributors

@milohiss

---

title: bug(pulse): flock FD 9 inheritance regression — 9>&- fix is structurally incomplete, recovery mechanism has fuser parsing bug (Linux)
body:
## Description

The flock FD 9 inheritance bug from GH#18094 is still occurring. Child processes spawned by git commands during pulse cycles inherit FD 9 and hold the flock indefinitely, deadlocking all subsequent pulse cycles. The recovery mechanism from GH#18141 (Layer 2 inode recovery) also fails to trigger due to a `fuser` output parsing bug.

This is the fourth occurrence of this root issue. Previous fix attempts:

- **GH#18094** (PR #18105): Added `python3 -c "import fcntl; fcntl.fcntl(9, fcntl.F_SETFD, fcntl.FD_CLOEXEC)"`. Ineffective — `fcntl(F_SETFD)` operates on the calling process's FD table, not the parent bash.
- **GH#18264** (PR #18309): Replaced python3 approach with `9>&-` appended to child-spawning commands. Correct mechanism but incomplete coverage.
- **GH#18141**: Added Layer 2 self-recovery (inode recreation after 3+ bounces from non-pulse holder). Works in isolation but has a parsing bug that prevents it from triggering in practice.

## Evidence

**Observed on a pulse-enabled repo (Linux, systemd timer):**

The `bd` binary (beads — a git merge driver) was spawned by a git operation during a pulse cycle. It inherited FD 9 and daemonised:

```
PID 298770, PPID 2247 (session manager — parent pulse exited, reparented)
FD: l-wx------ 9 -> /home/rob/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.lock
Process: /home/rob/go/bin/bd daemon start
Started: Mon Apr 13 12:04:10 2026
```

22 consecutive bounces, pulse completely locked out for ~50 minutes, zero self-recovery.

### Problem 1: `9>&-` coverage is structurally incomplete

The fix from GH#18264 appended `9>&-` to specific child-spawning commands. Current coverage across all `pulse-*.sh` modules:

- Git commands **with** `9>&-`: **3**
- Git commands **without** `9>&-`: **44**

Any of the 44 uncovered git commands can trigger a merge driver (like `bd`), which daemonises and holds the flock. The `9>&-` approach is a blocklist model — it requires every current and future child-spawning command to be individually annotated. This is structurally unsound because:

- New git calls added to pulse stages won't have `9>&-` unless the developer knows about this requirement
- Git merge drivers, hooks, and filters can all spawn background processes
- `git pull`, `git worktree add`, `git push` (with pre-push hooks) are all potential triggers
- The requirement is invisible — nothing in the code communicates "every child-spawning command must close FD 9"

### Problem 2: Recovery mechanism `fuser` parsing bug

`pulse-instance-lock.sh:94`:
```bash
flock_holder_pid=$(fuser "$LOCKFILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
```

During a bounce, the current pulse process also has FD 9 open (from `exec 9>"$LOCKFILE"` at `pulse-wrapper.sh:1110`, which runs BEFORE the `flock -n 9` attempt). So `fuser` returns multiple PIDs — the orphaned holder AND the current pulse process:

```
fuser output: "298770 302558"
After tr -d ' ': "298770302558"
```

Then `ps -p "298770302558"` fails (not a valid PID), `flock_holder_comm` is empty, and the recovery condition `[[ -n "$flock_holder_comm" ]]` evaluates false. The recovery block is never entered.

Log evidence:
```
flock secondary guard: held by PID 298770302558302995302997 (unknown), bounce 1
flock secondary guard: held by PID 298770302558302995302997 (unknown), bounce 22
```

Note `(unknown)` — the `ps` lookup failed on every bounce.

## Considerations

This is an **architectural problem**, not a missing annotation. The `9>&-` blocklist approach cannot scale. Some alternatives for the maintainers to evaluate:

1. **Subshell wrapper for all external commands** — run everything through a function that closes FD 9 before exec. Allowlist model instead of blocklist.
2. **Don't use flock** — the mkdir-based lock is already documented as the "primary atomic primitive" (`pulse-instance-lock.sh:48`). If flock is supplementary and causes recurring deadlocks, its cost may exceed its value on Linux.
3. **Use `/proc/self/fd/9` with `O_CLOEXEC` via a compiled helper** — a small C binary that calls `fcntl(9, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC)` in the parent process (bash cannot do this natively). Would make FD 9 close-on-exec for all child processes without per-command annotation.
4. **Open FD 9 with bash `{fd}>` syntax** (bash 4.1+) and close/reopen around external commands — complex but keeps flock.

Separately, the `fuser` parsing bug should be fixed regardless of the architectural direction — extracting the first PID or filtering out `$$` would make the recovery mechanism functional.

## Platform

This is **Linux-specific**. macOS does not use the flock supplementary layer (`pulse-instance-lock.sh:88` gates on `command -v flock`). macOS relies on mkdir-only locking, which is not affected by FD inheritance.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.8.6
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: 2.89.0

title: bug(pulse): pulse shell stages create issues with origin:interactive — undispatchable after GH#18352
body:
## Description

The pulse process (systemd/launchd) never declares itself as headless. When pulse shell stages — post-merge-review-scanner, simplification, quality-debt — call `gh_create_issue`, `detect_session_origin()` in `shared-constants.sh` finds no headless env vars and defaults to `"interactive"`. This causes:

1. Every issue created by pulse shell stages gets `origin:interactive` label
2. `_gh_wrapper_auto_assignee()` sees "interactive" origin → auto-assigns the maintainer
3. GH#18352's dedup rule blocks dispatch: `origin:interactive` + human assignee = blocked

The result: issues created by automated pulse stages are undispatchable after maintainer approval (NMR removal) without manually swapping `origin:interactive` → `origin:worker` and removing the assignee.

## Evidence from this repo

Scanner-created issues in `marcusquinn/aidevops` itself carry `origin:interactive`:

```
#18636  origin:interactive  review-followup  source:review-scanner
#18623  origin:interactive  review-followup  source:review-scanner
#18621  origin:interactive  review-followup  source:review-scanner
#18620  origin:interactive  review-followup  source:review-scanner
```

These were created by `_run_post_merge_review_scanner()` in `pulse-simplification.sh`, which calls `post-merge-review-scanner.sh`, which calls `gh_create_issue`.

## Root Cause Chain

1. **No headless env var set at the pulse level**: The systemd service unit (`aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`) does not include `Environment=AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true`. `pulse-wrapper.sh` does not `export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true`.

2. **Worker dispatch correctly sets it, but shell stages don't**: `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1324` passes `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=true` to child LLM worker processes. But direct shell function calls (scanner, simplification, quality-debt) run in the parent process where no headless var exists.

3. **`detect_session_origin()` defaults to "interactive"** (`shared-constants.sh:796`): Checks `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` — none set → returns "interactive".

4. **Auto-assignment compounds the problem**: `_gh_wrapper_auto_assignee()` (`shared-constants.sh:847`) sees "interactive" → calls `gh api user` → assigns the maintainer. Even if the GH#18352 dedup rule were relaxed, the maintainer would still be auto-assigned.

## Affected Code Paths

Every `gh_create_issue` call in pulse shell stages is affected:

| Module | Calls |
|--------|-------|
| `pulse-simplification.sh` | 7 |
| `pulse-simplification-state.sh` | 1 |
| `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` | 1 |
| `quality-feedback-helper.sh` | 1 |
| **Total** | **10** |

## Why This Surfaced Now

Before GH#18352 (merged April 12), `origin:interactive` alone didn't prevent dispatch. GH#18352 correctly fixed the race where the pulse dispatched against tasks active interactive sessions were working on. But it also inadvertently blocks all pulse-created issues because the pulse falsely identifies as interactive.

The scanner's own `SCANNER_NEEDS_REVIEW=true` default documents the intended flow: create → NMR gate → maintainer reviews → removes NMR → dispatch. GH#18352 broke the final step for all pulse-created issues.

## Considerations

- **Not platform-specific** — `detect_session_origin()` is pure shell logic; same behavior on Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd)
- **Related**: GH#18648 (ever-NMR permanence trap) addressed a different angle of the same symptom class — bot-generated issues stuck forever
- **Related**: GH#18403 (t1984) added `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN` override for the sync-todo-to-issues workflow — same class of problem (a headless/automated context being misidentified as interactive)

### Potential approaches (for maintainers to evaluate)

1. **`pulse-wrapper.sh` exports `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` early** — the pulse is definitionally headless; cascades to all sourced modules and child scripts
2. **Systemd/launchd service unit adds `Environment=AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true`** — works but fragile across unit regeneration
3. **Each pulse stage sets `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN=worker` before `gh_create_issue`** — more targeted but requires fixing 10 call sites independently
4. **`sudo aidevops approve` removes `origin:interactive` and unassigns as part of the approval flow** — treats the symptom rather than the cause

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.8.6
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: 2.89.0

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/bash-fd-locking.md`
**Detected topic:** Bash FD Locking — Why flock was removed from the pulse instance lock
**Current size:** 58 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/bash-fd-locking.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)

title: t2052: review-followup scanner: GraphQL reviewThreads + diffHunk + refresh backfill
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

# Task Brief - t2052: review-followup scanner — GraphQL reviewThreads + diffHunk + refresh backfill

## Context

- **Session Origin**: Interactive (continues GH#18538, PR #18607)
- **Task ID**: t2052
- **Files**:
  - `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh`
  - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` (new)

## Background

PR #18607 improved `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` issue bodies to include full
comment bodies, file:line refs, and a Worker Guidance section. But running the
new scanner against PR #18343 revealed two remaining problems:

1. **Spurious issues**: every CodeRabbit finding on PR #18343 was already
   marked `✅ Addressed in commit 0d8fe9a` by CodeRabbit itself. The scanner
   currently has no way to detect resolved threads and files issues for
   findings that are already fixed. Issue #18621 is the canonical example —
   it lists 5 findings, all of which CodeRabbit had resolved in the same PR
   before merge. A worker dispatched against it would burn tokens "fixing"
   code that is already correct.
2. **No code context**: the issue body points at `file.mjs:495` but does not
   include any of the surrounding code. Workers have to open the file and
   scroll to the target line before they can assess the finding.

Additionally: ~10 stale issues (#18588–#18623) exist from the pre-#18607
scanner and have truncated 200-char bodies. These are still in the backlog.

## What

1. Rewrite `fetch_inline_comments_md()` to query GitHub's GraphQL
   `reviewThreads` connection instead of the REST `/comments` endpoint.
   GraphQL returns `isResolved` and `isOutdated` — canonical, bot-agnostic
   resolution signals that work for CodeRabbit, Gemini, claude-review,
   gpt-review, and human reviewers alike. Filter out threads where either
   flag is true.

2. Include the tail of the `diffHunk` field (~12 lines) in each inline
   comment block as a ```diff fenced code block, so the worker sees the
   code context the bot was flagging without opening the file.

3. Tighten `fetch_review_summaries_md()` to skip CodeRabbit's
   `**Actionable comments posted: N**` metadata reviews. Gemini's
   `## Code Review` summary reviews are substantive findings and must be
   preserved.

4. Add a `refresh [REPO]` subcommand that:
   - Lists open `review-followup` issues.
   - Extracts the source PR number from each issue title.
   - Recomputes the body via `build_pr_followup_body()`.
   - If the new body is non-empty, rewrites the issue body.
   - If the new body is empty (all findings resolved or outdated after
     filters), closes the issue with a comment explaining why.
   - Self-heals future regressions where the scanner's output format changes.

5. Add stub-based test coverage at
   `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` covering:
   - All-resolved threads → `build_pr_followup_body` returns 1 (no body).
   - Mixed resolved/unresolved → only unresolved threads appear.
   - diffHunk tail is included under each comment.
   - CodeRabbit `Actionable comments posted:` review is filtered out.
   - Gemini `## Code Review` summary is preserved.

## Why

- **Spurious issues waste tokens and dispatch cycles.** Issue #18621 is the
  worst case: 5 findings, all already resolved. Every dispatched worker on
  that issue will either time out or file a duplicate "nothing to do" PR.
- **Code context inline** eliminates one full file-read per finding, which
  is the single biggest token cost of the current workflow.
- **The `refresh` subcommand** fixes the stale backlog without manual
  close-and-recreate, and acts as a self-heal mechanism for the next time
  the output format changes.
- **GraphQL `isResolved`/`isOutdated`** is the canonical signal from GitHub.
  Per-bot markers (like CodeRabbit's `Addressed in commit X`) are brittle
  and don't cover Gemini, which never self-marks. Using GraphQL means the
  filter works uniformly across all bots now and in the future.

## How

1. In `post-merge-review-scanner.sh`:
   - Replace `fetch_inline_comments_md()` body with a `gh api graphql`
     call querying `reviewThreads(first: 100)` on the PR, filtering
     `isResolved == false && isOutdated == false`, then joining with
     the author-bot regex (`BOT_RE`).
   - Add diffHunk tail: `split("\n") | (if length > 12 then .[-12:] else . end) | join("\n")` wrapped in a ```diff fence.
   - Drop the `ACT_RE` filter for inline comments (redundant: all unresolved
     review threads are findings by definition).
   - Replace `fetch_file_refs_md()` with a GraphQL version for consistency
     so it sees the same set of comments as the inline fetcher.
   - In `fetch_review_summaries_md()` add a `select` that skips bodies
     starting with `**Actionable comments posted:` or `Actionable comments posted:`.
   - Add `cmd_refresh()` + wire it into `main()`. Key loop:
     - `gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label review-followup --state open --json number,title,body --jq '.[]'`
     - For each, regex-extract `(\d+)` from title after `Review followup: PR #`.
     - Call `build_pr_followup_body "$repo" "$pr"`.
     - On success (exit 0), `gh issue edit` only if body changed.
     - On failure (exit 1, no actionable findings), `gh issue close` with a
       comment: "All review findings on PR #${pr} are resolved or outdated as
       of $(date). Closing as superseded by GraphQL reviewThread resolution
       filter (t2052)."

2. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh`:
   - Follow the stub pattern used in
     `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-lib.sh` (stub `gh` via a
     shell function that returns canned JSON from fixtures).
   - Create fixtures under
     `.agents/scripts/tests/fixtures/post-merge-review-scanner/`:
     - `pr-all-resolved.json` — 3 threads, all `isResolved: true`
     - `pr-mixed.json` — 2 resolved, 2 unresolved
     - `pr-with-diffhunk.json` — 1 unresolved thread, 20-line diffHunk
     - `coderabbit-summary-review.json` — top-level "Actionable comments posted"
     - `gemini-summary-review.json` — top-level "## Code Review"
   - Export `PATH="$tmp:$PATH"` so the stub `gh` wins over the real one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_pr_followup_body` returns exit 1 when all threads are resolved or outdated.
- [ ] `build_pr_followup_body` output contains a ```diff block with the diffHunk tail under each inline comment.
- [ ] CodeRabbit `Actionable comments posted: N` review bodies are filtered out of the output.
- [ ] Gemini `## Code Review` review bodies are preserved in the output.
- [ ] `post-merge-review-scanner.sh refresh marcusquinn/aidevops` in dry-run mode prints the planned edits/closes without errors.
- [ ] Test harness at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` runs and passes (covers all 5 scenarios above).
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh` clean.
- [ ] One-off `refresh` run against `marcusquinn/aidevops` after merge updates/closes the stale #18588–#18623 backlog.

## Verification

```bash
# Lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh

# Tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh

# Live smoke test against PR #18343 (5 resolved threads expected)
bash -c 'source .agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh scan 2>&1 || true' marcusquinn/aidevops
# build_pr_followup_body marcusquinn/aidevops 18343 should return exit 1

# Dry-run refresh against aidevops
SCANNER_DRY_RUN=true .agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh refresh marcusquinn/aidevops
```

## Tier

`tier:standard` — narrative brief with explicit file references, two
functions to rewrite, one new subcommand, one new test file. Not
trivially copy-pasteable (Haiku), not novel design (Opus). Sonnet.

title: t2058: fix shellcheck SC2154 on install_brew/install_python in setup/_common.sh
body:
## Problem

`version-manager.sh release patch` preflight scans files changed since v3.8.8 with shellcheck and flags two pre-existing SC2154 warnings in `.agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh`:

```
Line 379:  if [[ ! "$install_brew" =~ ^[Yy]?$ ]]; then
                    ^-----------^ SC2154: install_brew is referenced but not assigned.
Line 592:  if [[ "$install_python" =~ ^[Yy]?$ ]]; then
                  ^-------------^ SC2154: install_python is referenced but not assigned.
```

These variables are assigned indirectly by `setup_prompt install_brew ...` via `printf -v`, which shellcheck cannot track through the function boundary. The warnings were caught by the preflight because PR #18728 (color-guard cascade fix) touched `_common.sh`, triggering a whole-file shellcheck run which surfaced pre-existing debt.

Caught during v3.8.9 release preflight from a session closing GH#18539.

## Fix

Declare each variable as `local` before the `setup_prompt` call in the respective functions. This both silences the warning AND makes scoping explicit (variable stays local to the caller instead of leaking to global namespace via `printf -v`).

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh`
  - Add `local install_brew=""` immediately before `setup_prompt install_brew` call (around line 377)
  - Add `local install_python=""` immediately before `setup_prompt install_python` call (around line 591)

### Reference Pattern

The existing pattern is: caller declares `local VAR=""` then calls `setup_prompt VAR "prompt" "default"`. Follow the same pattern for both sites.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh
# Expect: no output, exit 0
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/_common.sh` is clean
- [ ] `version-manager.sh release patch` preflight passes
- [ ] No behavioural change — the fix is a scoping declaration only

body:
_Supersedes #18458 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

**Parent tracking task** for the phased decomposition of `.agents/scripts/stats-functions.sh` (3,164 lines, 48 functions). The plan document and Phase 0 safety net have already landed; this issue exists solely to track the remaining Phase 1–3 extractions and to gate simplification / threshold ratcheting behind their completion.

This is a **parent-only** task. No code is moved by THIS issue. Implementation lives in child phase tasks filed sequentially as each prior phase merges. The `parent-task` label invokes the t1986 dispatch guard so the pulse never dispatches a worker against this issue directly — only its children are dispatchable.

## Why

- **3,164 lines** is the second-largest file in the codebase post-t1962, more than 1.5× the simplification gate's 2,000-line threshold.
- **48 functions** in one file means it routinely surfaces in `--complexity-scan` and creates noise in PR review.
- **Methodology is proven.** t1962 ran for 10 phases without a single byte-level regression; the same pattern applied to a 23%-sized file with cleaner cluster boundaries is a 3-phase project (Plan §6).
- **Minimal external surface.** `stats-functions.sh` is currently sourced by `stats-wrapper.sh` and `tests/test-quality-sweep-serialization.sh` only — verified by `rg -l "stats-functions"` in PR #18581. The orchestrator-change scope is therefore small.
- **Blocks threshold ratcheting.** `FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD` is currently 59 partly because of this file.

## How

The parent task tracks progress against `todo/plans/stats-functions-decomposition.md` (already committed in PR #18581) and files each phase subtask sequentially.

### Phase tracker

- [x] **Phase 0** — characterization safety net (test harness, `--self-check`, `--dry-run`). Plan §5, §6 Phase 0. Shipped as **t2044 / PR #18611** (`tier:standard`).
- [ ] **Phase 1** — extract `stats-shared.sh` (3 fns, ~120 lines). Plan §6 Phase 1. File as child task after Phase 0 deploy is verified stable. `tier:standard`.
- [ ] **Phase 2** — extract `stats-quality-sweep.sh` (23 fns, ~1,692 lines). Plan §6 Phase 2. File after Phase 1 merges. `tier:standard`.
- [ ] **Phase 3** — extract `stats-health-dashboard.sh` (22 fns, ~1,252 lines). Plan §6 Phase 3. File after Phase 2 merges. `tier:standard`.
- [ ] **Phase 4 (optional)** — clear the simplification gate and lower the `FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD` ratchet. Plan §6 Phase 4.

**Sequencing rule (t1962 precedent):** File Phase N+1 only after Phase N merges. Prevents workers from picking up phases whose prerequisites have not landed.

### Dispatch rules for child phases

Per the Comment 3 (2026-04-13T04:54Z) systemic fixes merged in PR #18625:

- Each phase child **must** include a "Worker Quick-Start" section inlining extraction commands, structural patterns, and signature gotchas. The t2044 worker failure (null output against ~4,900 lines of reference material) is the reference case.
- Each child brief **must** inline critical data rather than saying "see Plan section X" — workers reading 500+ line plan files to extract 50 lines of data waste their token budget.
- Plan-sketch function signatures **must** be verified against live source before filing each child task. The t2044 plan sketch had `_persist_role_cache` with 2 args vs 3 in source.
- **Phase 0-style decomposition tasks dispatch at `tier:reasoning`**, not `tier:standard`, when reference-material reading load exceeds ~2,000 lines. This is now codified in `reference/task-taxonomy.md`.
- Child PR bodies referencing this parent **must** use `For #<parent>` or `Ref #<parent>`, never `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves`. The parent stays open until all phase children merge. PR #18601 re-triggered the parent-task auto-close trap by writing ``Resolves #18458`` inside backticks inside the PR body — GitHub's keyword detector is not markdown-aware. Prevention is now live as the `parent-task-keyword-guard.sh` shipped in t2046 / PRs #18663 + #18664.

### PR conventions (reminder)

- Phase children use `For #<this-issue>` in PR bodies → no auto-close.
- Only the final phase child (Phase 3 PR) uses `Closes #<this-issue>`.
- See `templates/brief-template.md` "PR Conventions" for the full rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Plan doc `todo/plans/stats-functions-decomposition.md` committed (landed in PR #18581)

title: t2074: fix(aidevops.sh): guard getent call + add cross-platform command portability rules
body:
## What

`sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` fails on macOS with:

```
/usr/local/bin/aidevops: line 26: getent: command not found
```

## Why

PR #18686 (resolves #18646) added `SUDO_USER` → `getent passwd` home resolution to both `aidevops.sh` and `approval-helper.sh`, but only `approval-helper.sh` got the `command -v getent &>/dev/null` guard (line 33). `aidevops.sh:26` calls `getent` unconditionally when `SUDO_USER` is set and we are root, which is always true under `sudo` on both platforms. On macOS, `getent` does not exist, so the command substitution fails and `set -euo pipefail` kills the script before any subcommand runs.

The commit message for #18686 claimed `macOS unaffected: sudo does not reset HOME; getent not available (fallback to $HOME)` — but this is only true for `approval-helper.sh`, not for `aidevops.sh`.

Also, this is a specific instance of a broader gap: our `bash-compat.md` rules cover bash-version differences (3.2 vs 4+) but not **command-level portability** between macOS (BSD coreutils, no `getent`, has `dscl`) and Linux (GNU coreutils, has `getent`, no `dscl`). A parallel set of rules for command portability would prevent future regressions in both directions.

## How

### Fix A: aidevops.sh one-line guard

Mirror `approval-helper.sh:33` exactly:

```bash
if [[ -n "${SUDO_USER:-}" && "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] && command -v getent &>/dev/null; then
```

On macOS, `sudo` preserves `$HOME` by default (verified: `env_keep+="HOME MAIL"` in `/etc/sudoers`), so the fallback to `$HOME` is correct.

### Fix B: expand `bash-compat.md` → add cross-platform command portability section

Add a table covering GNU ↔ BSD ↔ macOS command divergences and reference canonical portable patterns (`setup-modules/shell-env.sh:33-38` has the dscl/getent fallback; `aidevops.sh` has `sed_inplace` and `_timeout_cmd`). The existing bash-compat.md is titled "Bash 3.2 Compatibility" — I will rename the H1 to reflect both dimensions.

### Fix C: regression test

Add `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` that greps `aidevops.sh` for unguarded `getent`/`dscl`/`gawk`/`gsed` calls and fails if any are found without a `command -v` guard or platform check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `aidevops.sh:26` uses `command -v getent` guard (mirrors `approval-helper.sh:33`)
- [ ] `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` runs without `getent: command not found` on macOS
- [ ] `bash-compat.md` has a new section "Cross-platform command portability" with GNU ↔ BSD ↔ macOS table
- [ ] `tests/test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` passes and catches the regression if reintroduced

## Context

- Originating broken commit: 401438c9c (PR #18686, resolves #18646)
- Symptom reproduced on: macOS 15 + bash 3.2.57 + sudo 1.9.17p2
- User sudoers has `env_keep+="HOME MAIL"` so `$HOME` fallback is safe on this host

title: t2083: fix(pulse-dispatch): Deterministic fill floor silently rejects all candidates without logging skip reasons
body:
## What

The `Deterministic fill floor` pass emits a `candidates=N` count followed by `Adaptive settle wait: 0 dispatches` with no per-candidate logging when every candidate is silently rejected. Observed on 2026-04-14 post-GH#18770 fix (first clean cycle of v3.8.17):

```
[pulse-wrapper] Early fill floor: dispatching workers before housekeeping
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: available=24, runnable=22, queued_without_worker=0, candidates=22
[0;32m[SUCCESS][0m Resolved opus -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (primary)
[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_triage_reviews: parsed 11 candidates from state file
... (11 triage skip lines) ...
[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_triage_reviews: dispatched 0 triage workers (24 slots remaining)
[0;32m[SUCCESS][0m Resolved opus -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (primary)
[pulse-wrapper] Adaptive settle wait (fill floor): 0 dispatches — skipping wait
[pulse-wrapper] Stage start: complexity_scan (timeout 600s)
```

22 candidates → 0 dispatched. No `Deterministic fill floor complete:` line. No `Launch validation failed`. No `BLOCKED`. No `skipping`. No `Dispatched worker PID`. Just silence.

## Why

The likely culprit is `_dff_should_skip_candidate` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:266`, specifically the `check_terminal_blockers` call which is invoked with `>/dev/null 2>&1` suppressing all output:

```bash
_dff_should_skip_candidate() {
    if check_terminal_blockers "$issue_number" "$repo_slug" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0   # skip silently
    fi
    ...
}
```

If `check_terminal_blockers` is matching every candidate (e.g., because of stale state from a crash, a bad regex match on a common substring, or a label check that false-positives), every candidate is silently rejected with no log entry explaining why. The only symptom is `candidates=N, dispatched=0` with nothing between.

Alternative root causes to investigate:
1. `check_terminal_blockers` false-positive on all 22 candidates
2. `dispatch_with_dedup` returning non-zero silently on all candidates
3. `_dff_process_candidate` hitting a `set -e` kill at a point before the function returns
4. `candidates_json` being truncated somehow between the `candidates=22` log and the while-read loop

Note: this is the same class of symptom the framework has now hit three times in one week (GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786) — a silent failure where a `set -e` or unchecked return swallows the error. Adding mandatory debug logging at each skip site would make this class of bug self-diagnosing.

## How

### Step 1: Add mandatory per-candidate skip logging

Every `_dff_should_skip_candidate` early-return path MUST log which check fired. Currently only `fast_fail_is_skipped`, the placeholder-body check, and the stub-body check log. `check_terminal_blockers` does NOT log from the caller — and the caller intentionally redirects its stdout/stderr to /dev/null.

Proposed: either (a) log `[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: skipping #{issue} ({repo}) — terminal blocker detected` unconditionally when `check_terminal_blockers` returns true, OR (b) remove the `>/dev/null 2>&1` redirect so check_terminal_blockers`s own log lines are visible.

Option (b) is cleaner — trust the helper to log its own reason.

### Step 2: Add a `PULSE_DEBUG` flag that bypasses the skip checks

When `PULSE_DEBUG=1` is set, `_dff_process_candidate` should log the candidate's labels, dedup state, and skip outcome before making the skip decision. This gives operators a way to debug silent-dispatch failures without modifying code.

### Step 3: Add a regression test

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` — constructs a mock `_dff_should_skip_candidate` that rejects all candidates, runs the dispatch loop, asserts that EACH rejection is logged. Catches future silent-failure regressions at CI time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `_dff_should_skip_candidate` early-return path writes a log line naming the check that fired
- [ ] The `check_terminal_blockers` call no longer uses `>/dev/null 2>&1` (its own log output reaches the pulse log)
- [ ] `PULSE_DEBUG=1` adds per-candidate debug output (labels, dedup-probe results, skip decision)
- [ ] Test `test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` exists and asserts every skip is logged
- [ ] Running the current cycle with `PULSE_DEBUG=1` reveals WHY the 22 candidates in the Early fill floor pass were all silently rejected

## Context

- Observed: 2026-04-14 03:22 UTC, first clean pulse cycle after v3.8.17 (GH#18770 fix) deployed
- Log file: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` byte offset 19879048
- Source files: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:266-295` (`_dff_should_skip_candidate`), `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:2263` (`check_terminal_blockers`)
- Same bug class as GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786 — silent return-code propagation failures
- Related: pre-merge checklist item 4 in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` (from PR #18785) warns about exactly this class

title: bug: _close_conflicting_pr auto-closes implementation PRs when a planning PR with the same task ID has merged
body:
## Bug: `_close_conflicting_pr` false-positive auto-close — confused planning PRs with implementation PRs

**Severity:** high — direct cause of lost work in production.

**Real-world incident (2026-04-14):** PR #18760 (`t2060: fix(task-complete-helper): move completed entries to ## Done`) was auto-closed by `pulse-merge.sh:_close_conflicting_pr` with the false claim:

> Closing — this PR has merge conflicts with the base branch. The work for this task (`t2060`) has already landed on main (via PR #18749), so no re-attempt is needed.

In reality:

- PR #18749 was titled `plan(t2059, t2060): file follow-ups from GH#18538 worker-is-triager session` — a planning-only PR that added `todo/tasks/t2059-brief.md` + `todo/tasks/t2060-brief.md` and one TODO.md edit. **No implementation files were touched.**
- PR #18760 actually implemented the fix in `task-complete-helper.sh` + `tests/test-task-complete-move.sh` + a 561-entry TODO.md cleanup. **None of that ever landed on main.**
- Issue #18746 is still **OPEN**.

The deterministic merge pass extracted the task ID `t2060` from PR #18760's title, fetched recent main commit subjects, ran `grep -iE "(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])t2060([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)"`, and matched the substring `, t2060)` in the planning PR's commit subject. The grep cannot distinguish a planning commit from an implementation commit.

## Blast radius

- `gh search prs --state closed --merged=false "has already landed on main"` returns exactly 2 PRs in the repo's entire history. One (#18584 / t2045) was a legitimate dedup. The other (#18760) was this false positive. **50% false-positive rate** on the only two cases that have ever existed.
- The bug will recur every time a planning-brief PR for a task is merged before the implementation PR for the same task — which is the **standard flow** under `claim-task-id.sh` + `/define`.

## Root cause

`pulse-merge.sh:_close_conflicting_pr` (lines 1097-1136):

```bash
matching_subject=$(printf '%s\n' "$commit_subjects" |
    grep -iE "(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])${task_id_from_pr}([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)" |
    head -1)

if [[ -n "$matching_subject" ]]; then
    work_on_main="true"
    # → closes PR with "already landed" message
fi
```

The function already knows that auto-closing the linked **issue** is unsafe (GH#17642 explicitly leaves issues open). But it auto-closes **PRs** based on the same heuristic — and a closed PR with no auto-issue-close means the issue stays open while the work that would close it gets discarded.

## Fix

**File-overlap verification before closing.** A real implementation duplicate must touch at least one non-planning file in common with the closing PR.

1. Change the commits fetch to return `(sha, subject)` pairs instead of subjects only.
2. When a subject match is found, fetch the matching commit's files (`gh api repos/.../commits/SHA`) AND the closing PR's files (`gh pr view ... --json files`).
3. Compute the intersection, excluding planning paths: `TODO.md`, `README.md`, `todo/**`, `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`, `*.md` files inside `todo/tasks/`.
4. If the intersection is **empty** → false positive. Do **NOT** close. Post an idempotent `_post_rebase_nudge_on_worker_conflicting` comment (modelled on `_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting`) and return.
5. If file lookups fail (network error) → fail-CLOSED: do NOT auto-close, post nudge, log warning. Better to leave a stuck PR than to lose work.
6. If the intersection has at least one implementation file → genuine duplicate → close as today.

## Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — refactor `_close_conflicting_pr` (lines 1074-1168), add `_post_rebase_nudge_on_worker_conflicting` helper modelled on `_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting` at line 1012.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh` — update the existing 3 tests to match the new TSV stub contract; add 2 new regression tests:
  - `test_no_close_when_matching_commit_only_touches_planning_files` — reproduces the #18760 false positive
  - `test_close_when_matching_commit_overlaps_implementation_files` — confirms genuine duplicates still close

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh  # 5/5 pass
```

Then post-merge: confirm the patch release ships and the bug cannot recur on a fresh run.

## Recovery for already-affected work

PR #18760 has been reopened (see comment trail). The branch `feature/auto-20260414-012652` is still on origin so the implementation, test harness, and 561-entry TODO.md cleanup are recoverable in full once this fix is in.

## Why urgent

Lost work in a rapid-pipeline framework is unacceptable. Every dispatch cycle that runs the buggy merge pass risks closing real implementation PRs as soon as their planning brief PR has merged. Patch release.

title: design call: classify _is_stale_assignment() gh-API failure path — fail-OPEN (current) vs fail-CLOSED
body:
## Follow-up: classification disagreement on `_is_stale_assignment()` gh-API failure path

The t2046 Deliverable A audit completed in PR #18765 classified `_is_stale_assignment()`'s gh-API failure path (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:455-457`) as **appropriately fail-OPEN** under deadlock-recovery semantics:

```bash
comments_json=$(gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}/comments" \
    --jq '...' 2>/dev/null) || comments_json="[]"
```

A duplicate parallel session (PR #18805, since closed as duplicate) independently reached the **opposite** conclusion: that this is fail-OPEN in the wrong direction, because:

> A gh-API failure → `comments_json="[]"` → no dispatch claim comment found → recover stale assignment → return 0 → unblock dispatch. This can undo `is_assigned()`'s protection on a transient gh-API hiccup, dispatching a duplicate worker against an issue that has a real active claim.

PR #18805's closing comment flagged this for follow-up but the issue was never filed — this issue exists to track the design call.

## What needs deciding

1. **Is the deadlock-recovery argument correct?** `_is_stale_assignment` exists to recover from worker crashes mid-dispatch. If gh API is down, dispatching another worker against a possibly-active issue is arguably better than letting the issue stall forever.
2. **Or is the duplicate-dispatch argument correct?** A transient gh API blip is more common than a worker crash. Failing CLOSED on API errors keeps existing claims intact and only delays dispatch by one pulse cycle (until gh recovers).
3. **Or both?** Differentiate API-error fail-modes by attempt count or timeout: first failure → fail-CLOSED (return 1, keep block), N failures over M minutes → fail-OPEN (recover stale).

## Context

- `_is_stale_assignment` is the only guard between `is_assigned()` and dispatch. If it incorrectly returns 0 (stale → safe to dispatch), the entire dedup chain is bypassed.
- The current threshold is 10 minutes (`STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS=600`), so a transient gh outage would need to span an entire pulse cycle to actually fire this path on every check.
- Test coverage: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh` covers the rest of the audit but not this specific path.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:445-499` (`_is_stale_assignment` definition)
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:455-457` (the contested line)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh` (where any new test would live)

## Decision

> 2. **Timestamp compatibility**: GitHub API timestamps may include milliseconds (e.g., `.123Z`), which the BSD `date` command (used on macOS in `_normalize_stale_should_skip_reset`) cannot parse with the provided format string. Normalizing the timestamp by stripping milliseconds (as done elsewhere in this file) ensures portability.
> 3. **Regex reliability**: Per the general rules, using the `^` anchor in `test()` on multiline strings can be unreliable. A simpler substring match like `contains()` is preferred for the initial filter.

> ```
> 
> <details>
> <summary>References</summary>
> 
> 1. Avoid using the start-of-line anchor (^) with the multiline flag (m) in jq's test function for regex matching on JSON strings from the GitHub API, as it may not work as expected. A simpler substring match can be more reliable.
> 2. In jq, use the fallback operator // to provide a default value for expressions that might result in null, such as min_by or max_by on empty or invalid inputs.

## Summary

Follow-up nits from interactive code review of the tool-name canonicalisation change in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs` (replacement of `mcp_` prefix strategy with Claude CLI CapCase canonicalisation).

## Why

The original change landed correctly but left stale naming and comments:

- `stripMcpPrefix()` no longer strips `mcp_` — it inverts the CapCase → lowercase mapping. The name lies.
- The new response-side regex matches any `"name": "..."` field in the SSE stream, not only `tool_use` blocks. The blast radius is bounded by `CANONICAL_TOOL_NAMES_INVERSE`, but the trade-off should be documented so the next reader doesn't "fix" it.

Single file: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs`.

- EDIT: `stripMcpPrefix` → `restoreLowercaseToolNames` (function + caller in `makeStreamPullHandler`).
- EDIT: expand docstring on `restoreLowercaseToolNames` to document the known trade-off (any `"name": "..."` field in text deltas is eligible for rewrite; blast radius bounded by the 9-entry canonical map; stricter lookbehind would need SSE chunk buffering).
- EDIT: update stale docstrings on `prefixToolNames`, `prefixToolUseBlocks`, `makeStreamPullHandler`, response stream wrapper, and `createProviderAuthHook` to describe canonicalisation (lowercase → CapCase) instead of `TOOL_PREFIX` / `mcp_`.

Function names `prefixToolNames` / `prefixToolUseBlocks` intentionally NOT renamed — scope creep for no behavioural benefit.

## How (Worker Guidance)

- [ ] `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `restoreLowercaseToolNames` docstring mentions the `"name": "..."` regex trade-off.

PR #18674 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/18674

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `prompts/build.txt`
section 6a). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

#### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call

Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply:
the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside
what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision
comment** with exactly these fields:

- **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real.
- **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs.
- **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were
  yours, with rationale.
- **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make
  (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended).

Then apply `needs-maintainer-review` and stop. The human wakes up to a
ready-to-approve recommendation, not a blank task.

> **Ambiguity about scope or style is not Outcome C.** Per
> `prompts/build.txt` "Reasoning responsibility", the model does the
> thinking and delivers a recommendation. Only escalate what is genuinely
> a maintainer-only decision.

   and any suggested change.

   is wrong, switch to Outcome A instead of burning iterations trying to
   satisfy a wrong suggestion.

Three-part fix for the race condition that caused PR #18956 (a wasted worker session) on issue #18950:

1. **Fix 1 (bug):** \`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\` — \`_is_assigned_compute_blocking()\` skips self-login when \`active_claim != "true"\`. In a single-user setup the pulse runner and the interactive user share the same GitHub login. The old self-login exemption fired before the \`origin:interactive\` check, making the guard ineffective in the most common case.

2. **Fix 2 (defence-in-depth):** \`full-loop-helper.sh\` \`cmd_commit_and_pr()\` — add a pre-PR closed-issue check. If the issue is already \`CLOSED\` when a worker is about to open a PR, abort and post an ops comment rather than filing a duplicate.

3. **Fix 3 (process docs):** \`AGENTS.md\` Auto-dispatch section — document that when implementing a \`#auto-dispatch\` task interactively, \`interactive-session-helper.sh claim\` MUST be called immediately, before writing code.

## Why

PR #18956 timeline:
- 15:37:55Z — Issue #18950 created: \`origin:interactive\` + \`marcusquinn\` assignee + \`auto-dispatch\`
- 15:40:06Z — Pulse DISPATCH_CLAIM fires (2 min later, same runner login as assignee)
- 15:41:10Z — Worker dispatched despite GH#18352 guard
- 15:48:29Z — Issue already closed by interactive session
- 15:49:15Z — Worker opens PR #18956 on closed issue

Root cause: \`_is_assigned_compute_blocking()\` line 718 — self-login check fires before \`active_claim\` check. \`blocking_assignees\` ends up empty → \`is_assigned()\` returns 1 (safe) → pulse dispatches.

## How

### Fix 1 — \`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\`

- EDIT: \`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:718\`
- Change: \`if [[ -n "$self_login" && "$assignee" == "$self_login" ]];\`
- To: \`if [[ -n "$self_login" && "$assignee" == "$self_login" && "$active_claim" != "true" ]];\`
- Update comment block above to explain the exception.
- Test: add Test 9 (self-assigned + origin:interactive blocks) and Test 10 (self-assigned + no label still passive) to \`.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-multi-operator.sh\`.

### Fix 2 — \`full-loop-helper.sh\`

- EDIT: \`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh\` — add closed-issue guard in \`cmd_commit_and_pr()\` after \`_validate_worker_claim\`, before \`_create_pr\`.
- Check \`gh issue view $issue_number --json state\` — if \`CLOSED\`, print error and post ops comment, return 1.
- Applies to all modes (not just headless).

### Fix 3 — \`AGENTS.md\`

- EDIT: \`.agents/AGENTS.md\` — "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" section — add mandatory rule for interactive implementation of \`#auto-dispatch\` tasks.
